title: What the gate lets through
prompt: The statements team reads only what passes the quality gate. Write `solve(transactions)` so it returns the transactions that load today: `transaction_id`, `account_id`, `amount`, `currency`, and the name of the first warn rule each one breaks in `warning` (NULL when none).
rules: Quarantine rules, with the largest share of the load each may set aside: `has_account` (`account_id` present) 10%, `known_currency` (USD, EUR or GBP) 10%, `positive_amount` (present and more than 0) 5%.

`known_status` is a fail rule: `status` is posted, pending or declined. Warn rules, in this order: `within_review_limit` (`amount` at most 2500.00), then `merchant_on_card_types` (a purchase or refund breaks it when it has no `merchant_id`; other types never do).

A missing value breaks a rule. Each rule decides once over the whole feed: `pass` when no transaction breaks it; otherwise a warn rule decides `warn`, a fail rule `stop`, and a quarantine rule `quarantine` when the transactions breaking it are at most its share of all transactions (exactly at the share still quarantines) and `stop` when they are more.
If any rule decides `stop`, nothing loads: return no rows. Otherwise every transaction that breaks no quarantine rule loads, warned ones included.
hints: Keep each rule as `(name, action, limit, condition)` and decide them in a loop first, with `failed * 100 <= limit * checked`.
`transactions.filter(F.lit(False))` keeps the columns and no rows. Build the warning expression first and select the same five columns, so an empty answer still has the right shape.
Build `keep` by combining `~F.coalesce(condition, F.lit(False))` of the quarantine rules, and the warning as a `F.when` chain over the warn rules.
explanation: The gate has two passes. First decide every rule from its counts, each with its own limit: `failed * 100 <= limit * checked` keeps exactly-at-the-limit in quarantine. If any decision is `stop`, the load is untrustworthy and nothing reaches the statements, so the answer is an empty DataFrame with the same columns. Otherwise filter out the rows that break a quarantine rule and label the rest with a `F.when` chain over the warn rules, so the first broken one wins. Warned rows are valid and load. Every condition goes through `F.coalesce(condition, F.lit(False))`, so a missing currency or status counts as broken instead of slipping through. With one limit for every rule, two bad amounts in thirty rows (6.7%) would be quarantined instead of stopping the load.
